name: Neural SDF Inference via Gaussian Pulling
aliases: Neural Signed Distance Function Inference through Splatting 3D Gaussians Pulled on Zero-Level Set
definition: A method that infers a neural Signed Distance Function (SDF) by pulling 3D Gaussians onto the SDF's zero-level set and constraining them to be thin disks tangent to the surface, allowing for robust surface reconstruction from sparse and non-uniformly distributed Gaussians.
summary: Neural SDF Inference via Gaussian Pulling reconstructs continuous 3D surfaces by jointly optimizing 3D Gaussians and a neural signed distance function, dynamically aligning Gaussians to the surface to overcome standard Gaussian splatting's discreteness and drift.
